title: CSS Reference
description: A compact reference of the selectors, properties, functions and at-rules covered in the CSS tutorial, grouped by topic, with syntax, a short example and the lesson that explains each one.

entries.name: element
entries.summary: Matches every element with the given tag name.

entries.name: .class
entries.summary: Matches elements whose class attribute contains the name. The everyday selector for styling components.
notes: Chain classes without spaces to require both: .card.featured
Specificity 0-1-0

entries.name: #id
entries.summary: Matches the single element with that id. Very high specificity; prefer classes for styling.
notes: Specificity 1-0-0: one id beats any number of classes

entries.name: [attr=value]
entries.summary: Matches elements by the presence or value of an attribute, with ^= (starts with), $= (ends with) and *= (contains) variants.

entries.name: A B, A > B
entries.summary: A space matches B anywhere inside A; > matches only B elements that are direct children of A.

example.code:
.menu a { color: #1d4ed8; }     /* every link inside */
.menu > li { font-weight: 700; } /* top-level items only */

entries.name: A + B, A ~ B
entries.summary: + matches B immediately after A with the same parent; ~ matches any B that follows A with the same parent.

entries.name: :is(), :where(), :not()
entries.summary: Group selectors inside one rule. :is() takes the specificity of its most specific argument, :where() always adds zero, :not() excludes matches.

entries.name: :has()
entries.summary: Matches an element based on what it contains or what follows it: the long-awaited parent selector. Supported by all current browsers.

entries.name: :hover, :focus-visible, :active
entries.summary: Match an element while the pointer is over it, while it has keyboard focus, or while it is being pressed. Order link states as :link, :visited, :hover, :active.
notes: Never remove the focus outline without a visible replacement

entries.name: :nth-child(), :first-child, :last-child
entries.summary: Select elements by their position among siblings. :nth-child() takes a formula such as 2n, 2n+1, n+3 or the keywords odd and even.
notes: :nth-of-type() counts only siblings of the same element type

entries.name: :checked, :disabled, :user-invalid
entries.summary: Match form controls by state: ticked, disabled, required, or invalid after the user has interacted with the field.
notes: :invalid is true before the user types anything; :user-invalid waits for interaction

entries.name: ::before, ::after
entries.summary: Generate a box as the first or last child of an element. The box exists only if the rule sets content.
notes: Decoration only: screen readers handle generated text inconsistently

entries.name: ::marker, ::first-letter, ::selection
entries.summary: Style the bullet or number of a list item, the first letter of a block (drop caps) and text the user has highlighted.

entries.name: width, height, max-width
entries.summary: Size of the content area (or the whole box with border-box). max-width and min-width set limits that respond to the container.
notes: Inline elements ignore width and height

entries.name: padding
entries.summary: Space inside the border, painted by the background. One to four values, clockwise from the top.

entries.name: margin
entries.summary: Transparent space outside the border. Vertical margins of block boxes collapse; auto left and right margins centre a block with a width.
notes: Margins may be negative; padding may not

entries.name: border
entries.summary: Shorthand for border-width, border-style and border-color. The style is required; without it nothing is drawn.

entries.name: box-sizing
entries.summary: Decides whether width and height include padding and border (border-box) or only the content (content-box, the default).

entries.name: display
entries.summary: The type of box an element generates: block, inline, inline-block, none, flex, grid, flow-root or contents.
notes: display: none also hides from screen readers; visibility: hidden keeps the space

entries.name: color
entries.summary: The text colour, inherited by descendants. The keyword currentColor reuses it for borders, outlines and SVG fills.

entries.name: #hex, rgb(), hsl()
entries.summary: Three ways to write a colour. Modern rgb() and hsl() use spaces between channels and a slash before the alpha value.
notes: An alpha channel affects one colour; the opacity property fades the whole element

entries.name: background
entries.summary: Shorthand for background-color, -image, -repeat, -position and -size. Omitted longhands are reset, including the colour.
notes: url() paths resolve relative to the CSS file

entries.name: linear-gradient(), radial-gradient()
entries.summary: Generated images for background-image. Several can be layered with commas; the first is painted on top.

entries.name: border-radius
entries.summary: Rounds the corners of the border and background. 50% on a square makes a circle; a very large value makes a pill.

entries.name: box-shadow
entries.summary: One or more shadows: x offset, y offset, blur, optional spread and colour. inset draws the shadow inside the box.

entries.name: font-family
entries.summary: An ordered list of typefaces; the browser uses the first one available. End with a generic family such as sans-serif.

entries.name: font-size, font-weight
entries.summary: Size (best in rem) and weight from 100 to 900, where 400 is normal and 700 is bold.
notes: The font shorthand needs at least a size and a family and resets what you omit

entries.name: line-height
entries.summary: Distance between baselines. Write a unitless number so every element gets a value proportional to its own font size.

entries.name: text-align, text-decoration, text-transform
entries.summary: Horizontal alignment, underlines and strike-throughs, and case transformation such as uppercase.

entries.name: @font-face
entries.summary: Loads a web font from a file and gives it a family name. Use woff2 and font-display: swap to avoid invisible text while loading.

entries.name: position, top / right / bottom / left, inset
entries.summary: static (default), relative (offset, keeps its space), absolute (removed, placed from the nearest positioned ancestor), fixed (viewport) or sticky (sticks at a threshold within its parent).
notes: Offsets do nothing on position: static

entries.name: z-index
entries.summary: Stacking order of positioned elements (and flex or grid items) within the same stacking context; higher values are in front.
notes: opacity below 1, transform and filter create new stacking contexts

entries.name: display: flex, flex-direction, flex-wrap
entries.summary: Makes the children flex items laid out along one axis. flex-direction chooses row or column; flex-wrap allows several lines.

entries.name: justify-content, align-items
entries.summary: justify-content distributes items along the main axis; align-items aligns them on the cross axis. Both set to center is the centring recipe.
notes: align-self overrides align-items for one item

entries.name: gap
entries.summary: Space between flex items or grid tracks, with nothing at the outer edges. One value for both directions or row-gap column-gap.

entries.name: flex
entries.summary: Shorthand for flex-grow, flex-shrink and flex-basis. flex: 1 shares space equally, flex: none keeps the item's size.
notes: Items shrink by default; use flex: none to stop them

entries.name: display: grid
entries.summary: Makes the children grid items placed into rows and columns defined on the container.

entries.name: grid-template-columns, grid-template-rows
entries.summary: Track sizes in lengths, percentages, auto or fr (fractions of free space). repeat(), minmax() and auto-fit build responsive grids.
notes: 1fr cannot shrink below its content; use minmax(0, 1fr) when content may be wide

entries.name: grid-column, grid-row
entries.summary: Place an item by line numbers: start / end, span n, or -1 for the last line.

entries.name: grid-template-areas, grid-area
entries.summary: Draw the layout as strings of area names on the container and assign items to areas by name. Redraw inside a media query for other screens.

entries.name: @media
entries.summary: Applies rules only when a condition holds: viewport width (min-width or the range syntax), print, or user preferences such as dark mode and reduced motion.
notes: Write mobile styles as the default and add rules as the viewport grows

entries.name: @container, container-type
entries.summary: Rules that react to the size of an ancestor declared as a container, so a component adapts to the space it gets rather than to the viewport.

entries.name: calc(), min(), max(), clamp()
entries.summary: Arithmetic on values, even with mixed units. clamp(min, preferred, max) keeps a fluid value within limits.
notes: Put spaces around + and - inside calc()

entries.name: px, rem, em, %, vw, vh, dvh, ch
entries.summary: px is fixed; rem follows the root font size; em the current font size; % the containing block; vw and vh the viewport; dvh the visible viewport on phones; ch the width of a zero.
notes: Write line-height as a unitless number
0 needs no unit

entries.name: transition
entries.summary: Animates a property when its value changes: property, duration, timing function and optional delay. Declare it on the base state so both directions animate.
notes: display and height: auto cannot be transitioned by default
Prefer transform and opacity for smooth motion

entries.name: @keyframes, animation
entries.summary: Define a sequence of steps and play it with the animation shorthand: name, duration, timing, delay, iteration count, direction, fill mode.
notes: Respect @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)

entries.name: --name, var()
entries.summary: Custom properties hold reusable values. Declare them on :root or any element, read them with var(), and give var() a fallback for undefined names.
notes: They inherit, so overriding one on a component rethemes everything inside it
A defined but unsuitable value makes the property fall back to its initial value, not to the var() fallback

entries.name: !important, inherit, initial, unset, revert, @layer
entries.summary: Tools that interact with the cascade: !important reverses priority, the four keywords reset a property explicitly, and @layer orders groups of rules independently of specificity.
notes: Rules outside any layer beat all layered rules
Keep !important for utility classes that must win by design
